title: Bring what you already have
description: Import an existing inventory.ini and group_vars, reuse your roles, then reopen and edit what you saved.
outcomes: Paste an inventory.ini and see how hosts in several groups are merged
Bring a group_vars file over as raw YAML, nested values included
Reference roles that already live in your repo
Reopen and edit saved components, and know where presets come back in

steps.intro: You rarely start from nothing. In this lesson I'll take an existing Ansible setup, its inventory, its group_vars and its roles, and bring it into kikx without retyping a thing.
steps.name: A project first. The name only labels it; the files you import keep their own names.
steps.inventory: Open the Inventory. Instead of filling rows by hand, we'll import the file you already have.
steps.importButton: Import inventory.ini reads a standard INI inventory: hosts, groups, :children and :vars sections.
steps.paste: Paste the file here, or pick it from disk with Choose a file. Look at the text: web1 is listed under [web] and again under [monitored].
steps.counts: kikx reads it as you paste. Four host lines, but only three hosts: the same web1 in two groups is one server, so it's counted once.
steps.replace: Replace hosts & groups swaps every row in the form for the imported ones. It doesn't merge with rows already there, so import first and tweak afterwards.
steps.merged: Here is web1: a single row in both web and monitored, with its address and user kept. Edit it once and every group follows.
steps.writtenBack: When kikx writes the file back, the connection details sit under the first group only. Under [monitored], web1 is listed by name, exactly as Ansible expects.
steps.addInventory: Add it to the project. The [db:vars] section came along too, as vars of the db group.
steps.groupVars: Next, the group_vars folder. Most repos keep a group_vars/web.yml with real structure in it: lists and nested maps.
steps.groupName: Type the group the file belongs to. The suggestions now come from the inventory you just imported.
steps.groupPath: The line below shows the exact path kikx will write. If your repo uses group_vars/web/main.yml, tick Folder layout to match it.
steps.yamlMode: Key / value rows only hold flat settings. For a real file, switch to YAML mode.
steps.yamlPaste: Paste the file as it is. Lists of sites, nested keys, all fine.
steps.yamlAsIs: The preview shows it written unchanged. kikx doesn't reformat or reorder your YAML, so the diff in your repo stays clean.
steps.addKey: Your turn: add one more setting on a new line at the end of the YAML, app_env: production. Watch it appear in the preview.
steps.addVars: Add the group vars to the project.
steps.playbook: Now roles. You probably have a roles folder already, full of work you don't want to redo. A playbook only needs their names.
steps.playbookName: Name the playbook file the way it's called in your repo,
steps.playHosts: and pick the group it runs on: web, straight from the imported inventory.
steps.role: Now type a role name, the folder name under roles/. kikx doesn't need its tasks; it just references it.
steps.roleWritten: The role is in the playbook. Ansible will find it in your roles/ folder when it runs.
steps.roleChecks: Checks will note that kikx doesn't vendor this role. For roles already in your repo, ignore that note; for new ones, it can scaffold an empty role for you.
steps.reopenWhy: Imports are rarely perfect the first time. Anything you saved stays editable: open it from the project panel.
steps.editHost: Say web2 moved to a new address. Here is its row, as imported.
steps.editPreview: The preview already shows the new address.
steps.saveChanges: Save changes updates the same component in place. You still have one inventory, not a copy.
steps.reopenVars: Your turn: open the group vars you saved earlier from the project panel, by clicking its row.
steps.reopened: Everything you pasted is back, ready to edit. Any row in the project panel works the same way.
steps.export: All of this lives in your browser. To carry it elsewhere, Export also offers a preset: one file that holds the whole project.
steps.openPreset: Next time, Open a preset here on the home page takes that file and brings every component back, ready to edit.
steps.done: That's it: your inventory, your group_vars and your roles are in kikx, and nothing had to be retyped. Look around, or go back to your own project.

checks.keyTyped: app_env: production is in the YAML

recap: Import inventory.ini replaces the host and group rows; a host in several groups becomes one row.
YAML mode takes a group_vars file as is, lists and nested maps included.
Roles already in your repo are referenced by name; Checks can scaffold the missing ones.
Saved components reopen from the project panel, and a preset brings a whole project back from the home page.

demo.ini:
[web]
web1 ansible_host=10.0.0.11 ansible_user=deploy
web2 ansible_host=10.0.0.12 ansible_user=deploy

[db]
db1 ansible_host=10.0.0.21

[monitored]
web1

[db:vars]
ansible_python_interpreter=/usr/bin/python3
demo.yaml:
nginx_worker_processes: auto
nginx_sites:
  - name: shop
    port: 443
    tls: true
  - name: admin
    port: 8443
    tls: true
demo.yamlWithKey:
nginx_worker_processes: auto
nginx_sites:
  - name: shop
    port: 443
    tls: true
  - name: admin
    port: 8443
    tls: true
app_env: production
